top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one clean, checkable mechanism: at the magic wavelength the lattice light shift cancels in the clock transition, so many atoms can be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime and the statistical gain is used without a systematic penalty. This is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, the error budget is physically understood, independent laboratories reproduce 10^-18 comparisons after twenty years, and it yields concrete physics (millimetre-scale redshift, constant-drift and dark-matter bounds). Katori (invention) and Ye (realisation at the accuracy frontier) give a defensible two-name allocation, though other groups' contributions are omitted; an award is still preferable to none.
